detail.longDescription:
I used to be chained to my laptop all day just to manage my self-hosted servers
or fix minor issues, and I hated waiting until I got back home to handle things.
I wanted the freedom to manage my infrastructure from anywhere straight from my
phone without trusting third-party cloud relays. I built VPSPilot
[https://vpspilot.app/] as a native Kotlin Android SSH client for my own daily
workflow. A few things I focused on: - Zero Proxies / Direct Connection: No
middleman servers or cloud accounts—your phone talks directly to your own hosts
over standard SSH. - Hardware Key Isolation: SSH private keys are locked inside
Android’s hardware-backed Keystore/TEE chip so they aren’t exposed or handed
over to anyone else. - Task Automation & Secret Handling: Automates my routine
sysadmin tasks and custom workflows so I don’t have to keep typing repetitive
commands on a phone keyboard, while keeping secrets from being typed raw into
the console. AI Disclosure: Built by me as a solo project for my own daily
server management workflow. I drove the core architecture, handled all testing,
and managed the device/Keystore implementation, while using an AI assistant for
syntax help, debugging routine exceptions, and cleaning up documentation.
